ideas.title: Crank it till the wire glows
ideas.critique: The glowing and burning wire was already shown in 'Where I rushed it'. What is new is the generator: back-EMF from the measured stator, a crank that gets heavier with current, and a hand the player has to pace. That closed loop of torque, current and heat makes it a skill instead of a show, and it actually measures the hand-power number the windmill needs. It falls back to a repeat if the crank is a key that sets omega with no torque coming back, or if the film is just a wire on a slab again.

ideas.title: Gear it, ride it: the dune run
ideas.critique: It hands the cart's real physics to the player as a choice the solver answers, and that is the dune step itself. But with three pinions and three loads it is a nine-cell menu, and once you have seen every ending there is not much left to master. The 'friends push' ending is a reaction, not a mechanic.

ideas.title: The motor sings its speed
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: Pitch taken from pegs times rev/s is honest and new for the machines, and hearing a stall coming is a real thing to learn. As pitched, though, these are oscillators keyed to state variables, not sound solved from the parts, and the island already has solved notes, so this is a step down in realism for its own medium.

ideas.title: Lumi takes the seat
ideas.critique: Rider mass in the dynamics is one number added to the cart, and the strained face is a look. The seat and the hand on the lever are the parts that count, but only if the IK really drives the switch rather than posing next to it.

ideas.title: The first lead plate fizzes
ideas.critique: It builds a core part of the big goal (the accumulator), with real electrochemistry, and Planté forming, where longer charging holds more, gives the player a reason to come back. The danger is another jar left alone on a bench under a fixed camera, and Butler-Volmer with lead's constants typed in is a rig for one couple unless the solver takes any electrodes.

ideas.title: A windmill on the crest
ideas.critique: Blade element momentum in the solved wind, with sail area as a choice and a runaway in a gale, is real engineering for the 'yesterday's wind' part of the goal. It is a big build, though, and without the dynamo it is a turning prop on a dune. A first session that only makes the sails turn would score like the land yacht still.

ideas.title: Tug of war with the cart
ideas.critique: The payoff is a friends' shoving gag. Friction from footing against a torque curve is one balance of forces that the dune climb already contains.

ideas.title: A real oak stump for the winch
ideas.nearest: A wheel you can see through
same_form: A wheel you can see through
ideas.critique: It is the fourth prop-reskin post in a short stretch: nothing moves or plays differently. Better materials belong inside a session that does something, not as its own post.

ideas.title: The cart at night with its own lamp
ideas.critique: A clay lamp at dusk by the motor again, this time moving. Driving by what the lamp reaches is a mood, not a mechanic, and the flame is a point light, not a simulation.

ideas.title: The commutator jams the owl
ideas.critique: It is the most absurd link here, and it is nerdy in a good way: the motor's sparks become a stealth tool. But owls do not hear radio. Unless the noise is the audible crackle, carried through a real sound field to a creature that really hunts by ear, it is a scripted confusion animation.
